name: Hawaii
agency: Hawaii Department of Transportation (HDOT); driver licensing is run by the county licensing offices

teen.nightLimit: Provisional license: 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. only with a licensed parent or guardian in the seat beside the driver, except documented work, school-sanctioned event or emergency (HRS 286-102.6)
teen.passengerLimit: Provisional license: no more than one person under 18 unless household member (or household member's foster/hanai child), unless a licensed parent or guardian is along (HRS 286-102.6)
teen.phone: All drivers: no use of a mobile electronic device while driving (hand-held). Under 18: no hands-free device either, except a 911 call. Fine $300, $400 in a school zone or construction area (HRS 291C-137).

bac.under21: any measurable amount (HRS 291E-64); the 0.02 threshold appears only in secondary sources

notes: Knowledge test length and pass mark not confirmed: third-party sites say 30 questions, but disagree on pass (24 or 25 correct). Left null.
Supervised hours: one secondary source says 50 hours including 10 at night; another says HDOT sets no minimum. Left null; not used in questions.
Permit supervisor: licensed driver at least 21, in the front passenger seat (secondary, dmvroads). Some sources add 3 years licensed; not used.
Written test offered in 14 languages including English, Hawaiian, Spanish, Japanese, Ilocano, Chinese (HDOT announcement reported 2015; list may have changed).
Move over (HRS 291C-27): slow to a safe speed and move to the adjacent lane if safe; covers police, fire, EMS, ocean safety, tow trucks and some state/county vehicles (Hawaii Police Dept.).

School bus: on a road divided by a physical barrier, all lanes on the same side as the bus must stop (Hawaii Police Dept. release, 2009, citing HRS 291C-95). Opposite-direction rule only from secondary sources.
